newsitem.title: POLAND: PBR interested in joining a banking group.
newsitem.headline: PBR interested in joining a banking group.

text.p: The sale of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) next year could become an opportunity for banks interested in buying it to form a financial group, the head of the Polish Development Bank (PBR) said on Wednesday.
"I believe that the PBK privatisation could become an important element of building another capital group," Mieczyslaw Groszek told Reuters in an interview.
He said that PBR, a mid-sized investment bank, would consider joining a larger financial group, as a way of strengthening its market position.
"I see a chance of a formal establishment of a consortium, even though I am not able to say now who would join it and on what conditions," Groszek said.
Last month the treasury raised the share capital of PBK, slated for sale in April 1997, by handing over 32.9 percent of its shares in PBR.
Earlier PBK bought 21.5 percent of another listed bank Kredyt Bank.
Groszek said that by setting up a group its members might boost their chances in bidding for up to 65 percent of PBK shares offered by the Finance Ministry.
"It seems that (having a group) could be a reason for the Finance Ministry to accept the consortium's bid," he said.

It is not yet clear which Polish financial institutions would be willing to form such a group but some media mentioned, along with PBR and Kredyt Bank, Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA (BPH) and the listed insurer TUiR Warta SA.
On Thursday Warta shareholders will vote on a planned new share issue to be offered to Kredyt Bank, BPH, PBK and two Warta's minority shareholders.
So far only Kredyt Bank has confirmed its interest in the new issue.

Groszek said PBR, which last week placed a $50 million Eurobond issue, would not use the proceeds from the issue to finance a possible purchase of PBK shares because such a strategic investment would require longer-term financing.
PBR had a net profit of 22.2 million zlotys after the first three quarters of this year, up 65.3 percent against the same period last year.
